header.summary: Name winegcc's temp directory deterministically, for reproducible builds
header.upstream: no (worth offering: it only changes winegcc's temp directory name)
header.why:
winegcc links each PE file from a spec object in a temp directory named
after the time and pid (tools.h make_temp_dir). lld-link records that path in
the PDB, and the PDB's hash becomes the PE file's debug GUID and, with
-Brepro, its timestamp. So every PE file differed between two otherwise
identical builds. Naming the directory after a hash of the command line makes
the path, and so the files, the same each time. compile.sh sets TMPDIR to a
fixed path, so it doesn't depend on the build machine's user either.
The hash leaves out winegcc's own path (in the build directory) and the
--cc-cmd/--ld-cmd values (a compiler cache's wrapper instead of the
compiler), which differ between builds that should match: with them in,
builds with and without ccache differed in every PE file.
It doesn't change what Wine does at run time.

header.summary: Build the dwrite tests with -fno-builtin so they link with LLVM 23
header.upstream: no, not yet (the same Makefile.in is unchanged up to 11.21)
header.why:
LLVM 23 (our llvm-mingw) turns floor() of a value it knows is not
negative into trunc(). The dwrite tests import msvcrt, whose import library
has no trunc or truncf (Windows' msvcrt.dll doesn't export them), so
dwrite_test.exe failed to link: "undefined symbol: trunc". -fno-builtin stops
the compiler treating floor() as something it can rewrite, as Wine already
does for its own CRT (MSVCRTFLAGS). Only for layout.c, where floor() is used:
EXTRADEFS also goes to wrc, which rejects the option.
It changes only dwrite_test.exe (in the -tests release file).

header.upstream:

in WineHQ 10.0 to master and in CrossOver 25.1.
header.why:
macdrv_start_cocoa_app waits 5 s for the main thread to turn into a
Cocoa app. On a Mac with every core busy, under Rosetta, that can be

header.summary: Start a 64-bit program at its entry point when its random base was already taken
header.why:
since Wine 11, the server gives each 64-bit exe a random base in
0x7ff600000000-0x7ff800000000, as Windows does. When that range is
already in use in the new process, map_image_view() maps the exe
somewhere else (often 0x10000), but the image information keeps the
assigned address in map_addr, and virtual_fill_image_information()
computes TransferAddress from map_addr. The main thread then starts at
the entry point of the assigned address, where nothing is mapped, and
the process dies with a page fault on execute before any of its code
runs. On macOS that range also holds host mappings, Rosetta's among
them, so this happens about once in several hundred processes. After
mapping, set map_addr to where the image really is. 10.0 has no random
exe bases.

start.exe crashed at base+0x36a0 (its entry point) before Shadow at the
Water's Edge and Sea of Darkness started; explorer.exe at base+0xefa0

header.summary: Don't let the main thread and a GL thread change an OpenGL context's view at once
header.why:
A WineOpenGLContext's view, latent view and update flags are changed
by the GL threads (macdrv_make_context_current, macdrv_update_opengl_context)
and, for contexts added while their view wasn't drawable, by the main thread
in the content view's viewWillDraw, which calls
macdrv_update_opengl_context. Nothing serialises the two. Both can read the
same old view or latent view and release it, and the view is then released
once too often. Add one recursive lock around those changes. A GL thread can
hold it while it waits for the main thread (OnMainThread), so viewWillDraw
only tries the lock. If it's busy, the context stays pending and the view
asks to be drawn again.
It needs a GL context made current on a view that isn't drawable yet,
which Wine 11's framebuffer GL surfaces (EmulateModeset) cause when two
threads draw to one window: each gets its own surface and view.
Upstream winemac has the same code in 10.0 and 11.x.
Found while chasing a crash at objc_release+34 in Nancy Drew games
("Pattern A"), but it isn't that crash: an instrumented build logged no
pending-context update and no overlap in any of the games' launches,
crashed or not.

header.summary: Don't release a freed OpenGL context on the main thread after it's deallocated on a GL thread
header.why:
-[NSOpenGLContext dealloc] calls -clearDrawable, which
WineOpenGLContext overrides. Off the main thread the override runs [super
clearDrawable] in a block sent to the main thread with OnMainThread, and
the block retains self. When a GL thread drops the last reference, that
happens during dealloc: the main thread runs the block, OnMainThread
returns, the GL thread finishes freeing the context, and the main thread
then releases the block and with it the freed context. objc_release reads
freed memory and the process dies ("Exception c0000005 in system thread",
at objc_release+34). Whether it crashes depends on which thread gets
there first. The block now holds an unretained reference: OnMainThread
waits for the block to run, so the context outlives its use.
Also, -dealloc released the view and then [super dealloc] called
-clearDrawable, which released it again whenever the context still had a
view. -dealloc now clears the drawable first, so the view is released
once.
Upstream winemac has the same code in 10.0; why 11.x shows the crash more
often isn't known (Wine 11's wined3d may release contexts on its command
thread, which has no event queue).

header.summary: Report the user's registers for a thread suspended on its way out of a syscall
header.uncertain:
Linux has the same window (frame+0x70 before iretq) without the
extra system call, so there it should be rare; not tested there.
header.why:
SuspendThread reaches the thread as SIGUSR1, and usr1_handler saves
the context that GetThreadContext later returns. If the thread is in a
syscall it saves the user's registers from the syscall frame; otherwise it
takes the signal context as user code. It decides with is_inside_syscall,
which only covers the kernel stack up to the frame. On its way out of a
syscall, though, __wine_syscall_dispatcher points rsp into the frame
(frame+0x70, to load the user's rsp or for iretq). A suspend landing
there saved the dispatcher's own registers as the thread's context: rsp
on Wine's kernel stack, just below the thread's stack, and rip in the
dispatcher. Now a thread whose sp
is in the frame is treated as in the syscall too: its context is built
below the frame, not over it. (On 11.x the dispatcher also restores the
user's gs base from there, and the 11.22 patch runs leave_handler
afterwards; 10.0's dispatcher keeps gs on the TEB on macOS.) Other users
of is_inside_syscall are unchanged.

header.port:
to 11.21: GPT_ABI_WRAPPER is CX 26.3.0's: a plain asm() block with only .globl, because
Wine 11's __ASM_GLOBAL_FUNC also emits .private_extern, which would hide the wrappers from
libd3dshared. NtReleaseSemaphore's count is LONG in 11.21 (ULONG in 10.0 and CX 26.3.0), so
the sysv_/msthunk_ signatures use LONG. The NtSetEvent thunk sits after
NtSetEventBoostPriority. FLAG: 11.21 runs Windows code with GSBASE = the TEB and Unix code
with GSBASE = the pthread TSD (CX 26.3.0, on Wine 11.0, still keeps GSBASE on the pthread TSD

text.

header.programs:
Second Chance (an app that embeds Wine): wants its helper
processes run without a Dock icon or menu bar and without taking focus
header.summary: winemac: ActivationPolicy option; "accessory" gives no Dock icon and never activates
header.uncertain:
macOS can still activate an accessory process when its window is
clicked; the driver only stops activating it itself. With FullScreenNone,
an accessory process's windows can't use macOS's own fullscreen (a Space
of their own); Wine's usual fullscreen (a window covering the display)
isn't affected, but this hasn't been tested with a game run as accessory.
header.why:
A program run as a helper of an app that embeds Wine shouldn't put a
Dock icon or a menu bar on screen, or take focus from the app. The Mac
Driver "ActivationPolicy" value, read the usual two ways
(HKCU\Software\Wine\Mac Driver, overridden by AppDefaults\<exe>\Mac
Driver), takes "regular" (the default, Wine's behaviour) or "accessory".
The environment variable WINEMAC_ACTIVATION_POLICY, set to either,
overrides the registry, so a launcher can set it for the programs it runs
(installers during a build, say) without changing the prefix. With
"accessory", topmost (WS_EX_TOPMOST) windows also stay at the normal
window level, since the process is never active: TopmostFloatInactive is
treated as none, and -adjustWindowLevels doesn't raise them to its floor
for floating windows (above the Dock, level 21), which otherwise applies
whatever TopmostFloatInactive says.
macOS also shows an accessory app's windows over another app's fullscreen
Space, even while the accessory app is inactive; a regular app's windows
aren't. Of the collection behaviours tried on a native accessory window
(default, FullScreenPrimary, Managed, MoveToActiveSpace, Transient), only
FullScreenNone kept it out. So with "accessory", -adjustFullScreenBehavior:
clears FullScreenPrimary and FullScreenAuxiliary and sets FullScreenNone.
With "accessory", the process gets NSApplicationActivationPolicyAccessory
when it first shows a window, instead of the regular policy and the Wine
menu, and the driver never asks macOS to activate it. Its windows are
still shown. Any other value, or none, changes nothing.

header.summary: gdi32: per-program ColorDepth: the screen depth one program sees, and its palette at 8 bits
header.uncertain:
whether a program needs RC_PALETTE and SIZEPALETTE 256 at 8 bits;
Director doesn't.
header.why:
Some old programs (Director projectors among them) refuse to start, or
draw wrongly, unless the screen is 8 or 16 bits, and a Mac display is
always 32. AppDefaults\<exe>\Mac Driver\ColorDepth (8, 16 or 24, as a
string or a DWORD; there is no global value) makes GetDeviceCaps(BITSPIXEL)
on a screen DC answer that in that program. Only calls through gdi32 get
it: win32u asks NtGdiGetDeviceCaps itself and keeps the real depth, so the
bitmaps Wine makes for the screen stay 32-bit. Telling win32u too makes
compatible bitmaps 8-bit with Wine's fixed colour table, and pictures
drawn through them lose their colours. At 8 bits a program also reads the
system palette after realizing its own (Director asks for all 256
entries) to learn what its pixels will show as. Wine has no system
palette, so gdi32 notes the palette of more than 20 entries the program
last selected for the foreground and GetSystemPaletteEntries on a screen
DC answers as Windows would once it was realized: the 20 static colours at
either end, the palette's own entries between them. Without the value
nothing changes. The display modes Wine reports are unchanged.

Second Chance (an app that embeds Wine): shows a program inside
its own window
header.summary: winemac: HostWindows option; a native host application shows the windows
header.uncertain:
each present waits for glFinish. Windows of other processes as
owners aren't supported (v1).
header.why:
An app that embeds Wine wants a program's windows inside its own
windows, scaled or letterboxed as it likes, and the input back, without
the program putting windows of its own on screen. The protocol is
docs/app-embedded-protocol.md, its wire format
docs/app-embedded-protocol.h (copied here as wmh_protocol.h). With
HostWindows ("y"; HKCU\Software\Wine\Mac Driver, or per program under
AppDefaults\<exe>\Mac Driver) and WINEMAC_HOST_SERVICE naming a host's
Mach service, the driver does the handshake before Cocoa starts. If it
succeeds, each window's Cocoa functions send messages to the host instead
of making an NSWindow, window surfaces are drawn into IOSurfaces the host
is sent (up to three per window, each handed back by surface_release),
and a receive thread turns the host's input, focus, close and quit
events into the usual macdrv events. Without the variable, or if the host
doesn't answer in 10 seconds, the plain driver is used and an err: line
says why. NSApplication still runs (for the main-thread dispatch, event
queues, displays, the pasteboard and keyboard layouts), but the process
shows no window, Dock icon or menu bar of its own. The design doc said
no NSApplication; keeping it changed much less of the driver.
OpenGL (and Direct3D through wined3d, and DirectDraw wrappers that use
OpenGL) goes to the host as views: each client surface is a view of its
window, and framebuffer 0 of its drawable is remapped, in the GL functions
the driver hands out, to an FBO on an IOSurface from the view's pool;
each present finishes, sends the surface (bottom-up) and points the FBO
at a free one. Win32u, opengl32 and wined3d are unchanged. The context
is kept current with no view attached. The cursor goes to the host too:
a system cursor by its NSCursor name, an image as an IOSurface (the
first frame of an animated one), hidden; SetCursorPos and ClipCursor are
passed on, and the cursor position is the last one the host reported.
The host can ask for a window's size limits (WM_GETMINMAXINFO) and say
a resize is starting; the driver posts those as queries without waiting
and answers with window_min_max. Repeated identical messages aren't
resent.
Covered: the handshake, windows, GDI surfaces, OpenGL views, cursor,
size limits, keys, mouse, focus, close and quit. Not yet: animated
cursors, window shape and alpha, Metal and Vulkan, displays_get, the
resize-size query, and
window_get_frame as a call (the driver keeps the frame it last set or the
host last reported).

header.summary: winemac: in host mode, the displays and current mode come from the host
header.uncertain:
Host displays are matched to real screens: the first to the
primary, the others by overlap with the real screen's rect. Without
EmulateModeset, the real modes are still listed and can be set, including
ones taller than the host's display. Also without EmulateModeset: after
the host's display changed (1512x945 to 1440x900 in the test host), Wine
logged "No matching mode found 1512x945x32 @60" once, most likely
restoring the test program's temporary (CDS_FULLSCREEN) mode at exit, a
size the display no longer had; nothing visible came of it.
header.why:
With HostWindows (0069) the host shows the program's windows, and it
may show them on less than the whole screen: Second Chance keeps them
below a MacBook's notch. Until now the driver still took its monitors from
NSScreen and its current mode from CGDisplayCopyDisplayMode, so Wine
thought the screen was the full height, and Second Chance needed a helper
injected into Wine that changed what those calls return. Now, in host
mode, the driver asks the host (displays_get) when it enumerates the
displays: each monitor's rect and work area are the host's display, the
current mode's size is that display's size (refresh rate and depth stay
the real mode's), that size is listed among the modes, and setting it
changes nothing real. A screen the host doesn't report is left out. The
host's first display must be at the protocol's origin; when it isn't, or
the host doesn't answer or answers unsupported, the driver uses the real
displays, and a host that didn't answer isn't asked again by that
process (each unanswered call costs the call timeout). DISPLAYS_CHANGED
from the host already reached Wine's display-change handling, which
enumerates again. Plain mode is unchanged.

header.summary: Rosetta 2: make it notice code written into another process
header.why:
NtWriteVirtualMemory writes another process's memory with
mach_vm_write from wineserver, and Rosetta doesn't notice code changed
that way: the target keeps running its old translation. After the write,
toggle the executable bit off and on from inside the target
(NtProtectVirtualMemory on the process handle) so Rosetta retranslates.
Armadillo, the DRM in Big Fish games, writes "jmp $" (EB FE) over its
child's entry point, waits for the child to reach it, then writes the
original bytes back; without this the child spins on the stale "jmp $"
for ever and activation fails.

overflows the window. Wine 10.0 has no framebuffer surface, so this is

header.summary: Skip the int 68h/41h SoftICE probes that Wine's macOS code segment provokes (Armadillo DRM)
header.why:
On macOS Wine runs 32-bit code in an LDT code segment (cs 0x107), not
NT's 0x23. Armadillo, the DRM in Big Fish games, tells Windows 9x from NT
by the high byte of %cs, so under Wine it takes the 9x path and probes for
the SoftICE debugger with "int 68h" (and "int 41h"). On a real 9x without
SoftICE those do nothing; here they fault. In Armadillo's child process
the fault goes to its debugger (the parent), whose debugger thread is
meanwhile in WaitForInputIdle on the child, so the launcher stalls and the
game never starts. Only in that LDT code segment, step over int 68h/41h
as 9x would. On NT they'd fault, but no NT program runs in that segment
expecting that: the segment is what makes these checks misfire.

header.programs:

header.summary: Centre a fullscreen GDI picture under an emulated display mode, instead of drawing it at the edge
header.upstream: no (WineHQ master has the same code, checked 2026-11-16)
header.why:
under EmulateModeset, when a program switches to a mode whose shape
differs from the screen's, win32u stretches its fullscreen window's
visible rect over the whole monitor and keeps the window rect where the
scaled picture belongs; winemac masks the rest black. Two winemac bugs put
a GDI-drawn picture at the window's top-left corner instead, leaving an
unpainted band:
- WindowPosChanged stores swp_flags & WINE_SWP_FULLSCREEN (0x80000000) in
  the 1-bit data->fullscreen, which keeps the low bit, so it is always 0.
  Store !!(...) instead.
- The window surface is relative to the window rect there, not the
  visible rect. Offset it in the surface flush. Moving the content view's
  own layer (layer.position) has no effect, since AppKit keeps it at the
  view's frame, so a surface that doesn't start at the view's origin is
  drawn in a sublayer below the mask. Surfaces at the origin are drawn as
  before.
OpenGL and Vulkan output already gets the offset from win32u.
Seen in Bioscopia (Director 8, GDI, 800x600 on 2560x1440): the picture at
x=0 with a white band to its right.

header.summary: wined3d: keep the mapped range for Wine's own buffers, so streamed draws don't flush whole buffers

range (wined3d's streaming buffers and push constants, ddraw's execute

internal ones (every d3d8, d3d9, d3d11 and ddraw application buffer has

header.programs:
Webmaster (Tivola, a Director 7 projector): Director reports
"Handler not defined #baRegister", as its Buddy API Xtra (Budapi.x32),
which imports LoadLibrary16, is unloaded straight after it maps.
Bioscopia ships a budapi32.dll beside its Budapi Xtra that imports
LoadLibrary16, FreeLibrary16 and GetProcAddress16 (found by
tools/scan16; not run)
header.summary: krnl386: when LDT entries are refused, load without 16-bit support and fail 16-bit calls cleanly
header.uncertain:
what a program does when a 16-bit call fails; Budapi's
functions that Webmaster uses make none. A 32-to-16 thunk can only be
called after ThunkConnect32 succeeds, which it now can't, so the thunks'
own code past WOWCallback16Ex (which reads the 16-bit stack that isn't
there) shouldn't run.
header.why:
kernel32's 16-bit thunks (LoadLibrary16, GetProcAddress16,
FreeLibrary16 and the like) are forwarded to krnl386.exe16, so a 32-bit
DLL that imports any of them makes the loader load krnl386.exe16 and run
its attach, even if it never calls one. The attach loads the 16-bit
KERNEL, which needs LDT entries for its segments. Under Rosetta 2,
NtSetLdtEntries refuses them (0057), krnl386 ignored that, and the load
faulted on a segment that was never set up (Wine 11.22: a write to address
0xc22). The attach failed, and with it the importing DLL. Now the attach
first checks that LDT entries can be set, and if not, succeeds without
loading the 16-bit KERNEL or giving threads a 16-bit stack. A 16-bit call
made anyway then fails with an error in the log instead of a fault:
loading a 16-bit module (LoadLibrary16, LoadModule16, and ThunkConnect32,
which loads the 16-bit side of a thunk) returns 2, file not found, and a
call into 16-bit code (WOWCallback16Ex, which the 32-to-16 thunks go
through) returns FALSE. Before, both faulted in the same way as the
attach. Where LDT entries work nothing changes.
On 10.0 nothing needs to come before it: its x86_64 NtSetLdtEntries
always returns STATUS_NOT_IMPLEMENTED, as ntdll-rosetta-refuse-ldt-entries
makes it under Rosetta 2 on 11.x.

A build12 ntdll.so that logs each SIGSEGV showed the fault, the
first in the process: a write (err 0x6) at invoke_system_apc's
set_async_iosb (server.c:419; movl %edx, 0x4(%rcx), the Information
field of an IO_STATUS_BLOCK32) to 0x79ca5268, in a reserved page with
reserved pages around it (vmmap). The same in two runs. Wine 10.0 has the
same code; why Steam reaches it only on 11.x isn't known.

wine-mac-builds.

header.programs:
Steam's updater (11.22 on macOS 15): after "Update complete,
launching Steam..." a thread holding the loader lock stored a 32-bit
status block into a reserved, uncommitted page and hung; every other
thread then waited on the loader lock, so the updated Steam never started
header.summary: Don't fault in a system APC storing an async result into a status block that isn't writable
header.uncertain:
the APC's callback can also write the program's buffer (a read's
data); that isn't covered here, and didn't fault for Steam.
header.why:
When an asynchronous read or write finishes, the APC_ASYNC_IO system
APC stores the result in the caller's IO_STATUS_BLOCK (set_async_iosb). A
thread that is running its own code gets system APCs through SIGUSR1, and
runs them on the signal stack. If the status block is no longer writable
memory, the store faults there; the fault can't be handled in a signal
handler ("nested exception on signal stack"), and the thread never
returns to its code. The status block can be freed by the program, or be
on the stack of a thread that has exited, in which case the server gives
the APC to any thread of the process. Windows ignores a status block it
can't write. Now the result is stored with
virtual_uninterrupted_write_memory, which checks the pages first, and is
dropped with a warning if they aren't writable. Information is still
written before Status, as set_async_iosb does.

after their wineserver was killed
header.summary: Exit a process when its wineserver is gone
header.uncertain: macOS only (kqueue); other systems keep the old behaviour.
header.why:
A Wine thread only finds out that the wineserver has gone when its
next request fails (abort_thread), and the process ends with its last
Wine thread. A thread that only sleeps (a non-alertable Sleep is local),
renders, or waits in a macOS run loop makes no request, so after the
server died (killed, or crashed) such a process ran on with its windows
and open files, and an app embedding Wine couldn't tell its program had
gone. Now each process watches its socket to the server (fd_socket) with
a kqueue in a thread of its own, with every signal blocked, and exits
(status 1, "wine: the server is gone; exiting") when the server's end
closes. The server closes that socket only when it exits or has killed
the process, so nothing that should go on running is stopped.

with EmulateModeset in a fullscreen Space: a click anywhere in the picture

header.summary: Keep a click in a fullscreen Space from reaching the window's frame view
header.uncertain:
The arrow itself hasn't been seen here: a Screen Slots slot (a
background login) has no live cursor to look at. Other buttons
(rightMouseDown:, otherMouseDown:) still go up the chain.
header.why:
Wine takes a click in -[WineApplicationController handleEvent:], before

header.summary: Don't overrun the stack opening a database by a path without a backslash
header.uncertain:
The path held for a Unix name stays "<current directory>\<Unix
path>", as before; nothing found uses it to open the file again.
header.why:
MSI_OpenDatabaseW takes a path with no backslash as relative to the
current directory and built "<current directory>\<path>" with lstrcatW in
a MAX_PATH buffer on the stack, with no length check. A Unix path, which
Wine accepts anywhere a file name goes, has no backslash, so a long one
opened from a deep current directory ran past the buffer and overwrote
the caller's locals or return address with path text. db->path is now
allocated at the length it needs; what it holds is unchanged.
